summary: Amanda Chicago Lewis attends an SEO industry party in Florida expecting to meet villains who ruined the internet, but finds sympathetic, mostly powerless hustlers. Interviews with SEOs and with ex-Google and Bing figures show a long cycle of manipulation and Google crackdowns, now escalated by AI-generated content. She concludes that Google, as a profit-driven private company that controls online information, bears the deeper responsibility: it is Google's world and SEOs only live in it.
one_line: A Verge feature argues SEOs are less to blame for a degraded internet than Google, whose power and profit motives shaped the web, now worsened by AI spam.
key_facts: The author went to an alligator party hosted by Darren Blatt in Fort Lauderdale for about 200 digital marketers; the alligator was only five and a half feet long, not the advertised 10 feet.
Google has about a 90 percent market share in online search, and by the end of 1999 it was handling the majority of online queries.
Daron Babin began doing SEO in 1994, promoted offshore casinos and Viagra, charged $2,000 and then $5,000 a day as a consultant, and now mostly invests in cannabis and psychedelics.
Lars Mapstead helped start AdultFriendFinder, which sold in 2007 for $500 million; his car-themed Facebook pages reached 25 million followers and earned $120,000 a month.
Google changed its algorithm in 2003 before its IPO and made the Panda and Penguin changes in 2011-2012, devastating many SEO businesses.
Peter Kent, author of SEO for Dummies, says 80 percent of SEOs are scammers; most SEOs the author asked agreed it sounded accurate.
Bruce Clay is often credited with coining 'search engine optimization' and is called 'the father of SEO'; his agency never hires an SEO with less than a decade of experience.
Matt Cutts ran Google's web spam team, left in 2016 after about 50,000 emails to outsiders, and received death threats; SEOs' gifts to him were labeled 'possibly poisoned.'
Danny Sullivan, founder of Search Engine Land, became Google's public liaison for Search in 2017 and insists search results have improved and that rule-breakers produce 'spam,' not SEO.

Lily Ray says Google results feel different because of E-E-A-T (experience, expertise, authoritativeness, trustworthiness), adopted after the 2016 election disinformation panic, and because AI-generated content overwhelms the algorithm.
Ray says churn-and-burn AI sites can earn $50,000 or $100,000 a month before Google removes them, often run by people living in places like Bali and Chiang Mai.
Cade Lee, an ex-con who served time for securities fraud, now runs a construction company and quit adult-site SEO after learning his sites supported human trafficking.
Most SEOs interviewed said search results are better than they used to be, and most considered 2003 to 2011 the SEO boom years.
Google's founders wrote in 1997 that advertising funded search engines would be 'inherently biased towards the advertisers and away from the needs of the consumers.'
